title: The Watcher Problem

canonical_node.axiom: Observation requires three functions, not two, because every two-part exit fails to terminate the chain of observation.
definitions: Measurement problem: the puzzle of how a quantum object goes from being in many possible states at once to being in just one definite state.
Terminate the chain: to end the loop of cause and effect.
derivation: The measurement problem is stated as a question: why does observation require three functions instead of two
It is asserted that every two-part exit fails to terminate the chain.

boundary: Does not provide a formal proof or detailed derivation.

Does not address alternative interpretations or counterarguments.
